gaps.question: Do the applicable sources distinguish a send attempt, transport acceptance, endpoint delivery and human acknowledgment for a walk-in critical result?
gaps.jurisdictions_compared: AE-DU vs AE-AZ vs US/international comparators
gaps.source_evidence: S1-11.1.1 (p40); S1-11.1.3 (p40); S1-9.1.5.e (p29); AD1-PP.11.2.d (p13); G2-2.1 (p6); G3-task-status; G4-xdw-workflow-document
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: The Dubai instrument requires clear reporting to the patient and a record of the communication. It does not define delivery, receipt or acknowledgment as distinct states.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: The instrument does not say what evidence proves the communication occurred, nor whether a transport receipt is sufficient for the §11.1.3 record.
gaps.technical_consequence: A naive implementation records 'sent' as success and closes the case; the §11.1.3 record then documents an event that may never have reached the patient.
gaps.proposed_product_control: Separate ATTEMPTED / TRANSPORT_ACCEPTED / DELIVERY_CONFIRMED / CLINICAL_ACKNOWLEDGMENT_CONFIRMED / COMMUNICATION_DOCUMENTED states with forbidden conflation combinations (INV-1, INV-2).
gaps.global_comparator: G2 Worksheet 2.1 explicitly separates 'reported' from 'acknowledged' in order tracking; G3 models a task, not a delivery.
gaps.review_needed: no - both instruments verified, but a Dubai-scoped evidentiary standard was not located

gaps.question: Does the Dubai instrument require re-communication to the patient when a walk-in result is corrected?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: S1 §9.1.5(g) requires a corrected result to be identified as revised, with the date and time of correction, and both versions retained. §11.1.1-11.1.3 keep applying to walk-in patients.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: No retrieved Dubai clause states explicitly that the corrected value must be re-communicated to the patient, although the Abu Dhabi comparator (AD1 PP.11.3(b)) and the US comparator (G2 2.3) both require a distinct notification for amendments. Absence in the retrieved set is not proof of absence in the instrument.
gaps.technical_consequence: An implementation may suppress re-communication because a prior acknowledgment exists.
gaps.proposed_product_control: Corrections always open a new communication workflow requiring named human approval (requires_approval) and a fresh acknowledgment bound to the new revision (INV-8).
gaps.global_comparator: AD1 PP.11.3(b) 'the laboratory communicates directly with the ordering clinician'; G2 2.3 requires notification of changed results and a visible amended flag.
gaps.review_needed: yes - manual review of DHA circulars and the laboratory's own SOP required

gaps.question: Is there a fixed acknowledgment or escalation clock for critical walk-in results?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: Both instruments delegate timing to the organisation: DHA requires a critical-results policy and an internally defined turnaround time; the Joint Commission requires written procedures stating 'the acceptable length of time between the availability and reporting'.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: No numeric clock is fixed by either instrument. The retrieved set does not establish what a 'timely' communication means for a walk-in result.
gaps.technical_consequence: A system that hardcodes a deadline would be inventing a requirement.
gaps.proposed_product_control: The clock and escalation window live in an explicit institutional profile, labelled PRODUCT_DESIGN_CONTROL, and are shown as such in the UI and the audit record.
gaps.global_comparator: G1 EP1 requires the organisation to define the acceptable length of time rather than setting a universal limit.
gaps.review_needed: no - but the facility must still adopt and document its own clock

gaps.question: What authorises an alternative channel or alternative recipient when the primary channel fails?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: S1 §9.3.4 requires electronic laboratory reports to be secured; §9.3.3 addresses electronic signature and telephone provision of critical information to a physician. The Abu Dhabi comparator delegates the means of notification to the facility.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: No retrieved Dubai clause states which alternative channel may be used for a walk-in patient, who may authorise it, or what must be recorded. The documented search did not locate such a clause; this is not evidence that none exists.
gaps.technical_consequence: An implementation may silently switch to an unverified phone number or portal, creating a confidentiality and identity risk.
gaps.proposed_product_control: INV-9: alternative channels are blocked unless verified evidence or an explicitly approved institutional procedure authorises them; the authorising reference is recorded.
gaps.global_comparator: AD1 PP.11.2(c) defines the means of notification in facility policy, showing the comparator also delegates rather than mandates.
gaps.review_needed: yes - this is the strongest candidate gap for a facility-level review

gaps.question: Which results may be communicated directly to a walk-in patient?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: §13.4 states genetic results shall not be communicated to patients directly and shall be directed to the referring/treating physician; Appendix 3 lists genetics as requiring a prescription, which excludes it from the walk-in category in §11.1.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: The two provisions appear to conflict only when §11.1 is read without its scope. The conflict resolves on reading: genetic testing is outside the walk-in category.
gaps.technical_consequence: A system that matches on keyword relevance alone will retrieve §11.1 for a genetic result and communicate directly to the patient.
gaps.proposed_product_control: Scope gate: the policy agent returns scope_permitted=false with a §13.4 citation; the deterministic gate blocks any transmission for that scope and escalates.
gaps.global_comparator: n/a - the conflict is internal to the Dubai instrument
gaps.review_needed: no - resolved by scope; retained as a documented apparent conflict

gaps.question: Is there a UAE-wide instrument that harmonises critical-result communication across emirates?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: Dubai and Abu Dhabi each publish their own laboratory standards with different recipient models (walk-in patient vs responsible clinician) and different read-back provisions.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: No national harmonising instrument was located in this search. The DHA circular index could not be enumerated programmatically; this is an unverified search, not a finding of absence.
gaps.technical_consequence: A multi-emirate deployment cannot reuse one rule set; jurisdiction must be a first-class input.
gaps.proposed_product_control: Jurisdiction is stored on every case and every source; the retriever filters by jurisdiction and the audit agent flags any binding citation from outside the case jurisdiction.
gaps.global_comparator: None located - no comparator establishes cross-jurisdiction equivalence.
gaps.review_needed: yes - requires manual search of DHA and DoH publications and federal health legislation

gaps.question: Does an acknowledgment of an earlier revision satisfy the requirement for a corrected revision?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: The instrument requires a record of the communication and identification of the corrected report as revised. Nothing retrieved addresses whether an earlier acknowledgment transfers.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: Whether a corrected value that contradicts what the patient already acted on requires a fresh acknowledgment is not settled by the retrieved text.
gaps.technical_consequence: An implementation may treat the case as closed because 'the patient already acknowledged'.
gaps.proposed_product_control: No transfer: the acknowledgment must be bound to the current revision (INV-8); the configuration is explicit and testable in S2 and S5.
gaps.global_comparator: G2 2.3 requires notification of amended results with a visible amended flag, consistent with a fresh notification event.

gaps.question: Does an acknowledgment establish that the patient understood the advice to seek medical care?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: S1 §11.1.2 (guidance) directs the laboratory to advise the patient to seek further medical advice. The Abu Dhabi comparator requires read-back for verbal and telephone results.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: No retrieved source defines what evidence would demonstrate comprehension for a written channel such as SMS or a portal message.
gaps.technical_consequence: A system may present 'acknowledged' as if it meant 'understood and acted on'.
gaps.proposed_product_control: The UI states explicitly that acknowledgment means the message was opened and confirmed by a named human, not that it was understood; the case cannot record clinical resolution.
gaps.global_comparator: AD1 PP.11.4(b) read-back requirement exists for verbal/telephone only.
gaps.review_needed: no - a product-boundary statement, not a policy gap

gaps.question: What must a laboratory do to verify that a contact number belongs to the patient before sending a critical result?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: S1 requires secure electronic reports and a record of the communication.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: No retrieved clause specifies identity binding for a mobile number, or what to do when the number is shared or stale. The search did not locate such a requirement.
gaps.technical_consequence: A message may reach the wrong person, and the record will still look complete.
gaps.proposed_product_control: Contact reference is stored separately from the patient reference; an unverified-recipient state can be raised; the gate refuses sends whose recipient is not verified in the profile.
gaps.global_comparator: AD1 PP.11.2(d) requires identification of the individual notified, which presupposes identity verification.

gaps.question: Do existing interoperability standards model a patient acknowledgment of a critical walk-in result as a first-class event?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: FHIR Task provides a work-item status vocabulary; IHE XDW provides a workflow document that maintains a historical record of tasks and expects actors to handle race conditions.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: Neither retrieved profile defines an event type meaning 'the patient confirmed receipt of this specific result revision'. Task 'completed' refers to the task, not to a human understanding a result.
gaps.technical_consequence: Integrations may map a 'completed' task onto a clinical acknowledgment, which the standards do not warrant.
gaps.proposed_product_control: ResultRelay keeps acknowledgment as its own record with revision binding rather than deriving it from a task status; this is offered as a candidate contribution to the gap discussion.
gaps.global_comparator: G3 and G4 are the comparators themselves.
gaps.review_needed: yes - standards review needed before any real integration

gaps.question: How long must the communication record for a walk-in critical result be retained, and in what form?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: S1 §9.3.6 cross-refers retention to the DHA Guidelines for Managing Health Records, which were not retrieved or reviewed in this build.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: The retention period and format applicable to the communication record are not established by the sources actually reviewed.
gaps.technical_consequence: A prototype must not invent a retention period.
gaps.proposed_product_control: ResultRelay stores records indefinitely for the lifetime of the demonstration database and states that no retention claim is made.
gaps.review_needed: yes - the cross-referenced DHA instrument must be retrieved before any retention claim

gaps.question: What should happen when the delivery outcome of a critical-result message is unknown?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: S1 requires a record of the communication. The US comparator requires the EHR to track order and result status so that problems with delivery can be detected.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: No retrieved Dubai clause addresses an indeterminate delivery outcome, or whether a retry is required, permitted, or forbidden while the outcome is unknown.
gaps.technical_consequence: A retry may duplicate the message; a suppressed retry may leave the patient uninformed.
gaps.proposed_product_control: Explicit DELIVERY_STATE_UNKNOWN state; reconciliation required before retry (INV-4); idempotency keys prevent duplicate sends; escalation when uncertainty persists.
gaps.global_comparator: G2 2.1 order tracking is the closest comparator concept for detecting delivery problems.
gaps.review_needed: yes - facility-level decision with clinical governance sign-off

gaps.question: How long must the communication record for a notified critical result be kept, and who decides when it may be purged?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: Federal Law 2/2019 Article 20 sets a floor of 25 years from the last health procedure, and DHA HISHD/PP-12 §4.6.1 restates it as an entity obligation, reserving longer-retention decisions to the Executive leader/Medical Director.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: Neither instrument says whether a message log is itself a health information asset for retention purposes, or what the retention period is for the communication trail (recipient, channel, timestamps) as distinct from the result.
gaps.technical_consequence: The prototype keeps every run, message and audit row in one SQLite file with no retention or purge policy at all. It therefore satisfies neither the floor nor a defensible disposal rule; it simply never deletes.
gaps.proposed_product_control: Retention is a schema-level field: every communication and audit record carries a retain_until derived from the last encounter plus the applicable floor, and deletion is a named human action recorded as an event rather than a routine job.
gaps.global_comparator: No comparator used; the floor is set nationally.
gaps.review_needed: yes - retention of the communication trail (as opposed to the result) is inferred from the definition of a health information asset and needs facility counsel confirmation

gaps.question: How does a patient raise, and how does the laboratory receive, a report that a communicated result is wrong?
gaps.what_existing_sources_establish: Federal law requires the validity and credibility of health data to be protected against unauthorised amendment; Dubai requires accuracy at record level and requires entities to implement methods to receive patient feedback about inaccurate information; ST-28 requires a corrected report to be identified as revised with date/time and both versions retained.
gaps.what_remains_unclear: None of the reviewed instruments prescribes a channel, a response time, or an acknowledgment duty for a patient-initiated correction request. The prototype has no inbound path at all: a patient cannot report an error through it.
gaps.technical_consequence: The system can document that a corrected result was re-communicated, but cannot receive the signal that a correction is needed. Correction is only initiable by staff, so the Dubai feedback duty is unmet by the product as built.
gaps.proposed_product_control: An inbound correction-request intake that creates a linked case, requires named human adjudication, and never mutates the original communication record - plus an explicit acknowledgement back to the patient. Tracked as GR-14 in the gap register and NOT implemented in this build.
gaps.global_comparator: None retrieved that sets a channel or a deadline.
gaps.review_needed: no - the absence is established; the channel design is a facility decision

itu_y3172.implemented_component: Synthetic laboratory, transport and human event generators; scenario JSON event stream

itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: 7 scenario files, 51 ordered steps in total
itu_y3172.limitations: Sources are fabricated fixtures, not live feed handlers. No telecom data source exists.

itu_y3172.outputs: Persisted event row with seq, at, kind, actor, source_layer
itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: events table populated for every run; exported in the audit bundle
itu_y3172.limitations: Collector is in-process; no queue, no backpressure handling, no multi-tenant isolation.

itu_y3172.implemented_component: Normalisation, schema validation, scope and revision tagging of incoming events

itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: Every guard reads MachineContext; malformed agent output is rejected by Pydantic
itu_y3172.limitations: Preprocessing is rule-based; no anomaly detection on the event stream.

itu_y3172.implemented_component: Five role-scoped agents producing validated structured assessments
itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: Each agent has distinct allowed_fields and a distinct assessment contract
itu_y3172.limitations: Agents are deterministic rule engines in this build. No LLM provider is wired in; the 'model' analogy is structural, not statistical.

itu_y3172.framework_definition_source: ITU-T Y.3172 §8.1, p15 - 'applies policies to the output of the model node'
itu_y3172.implemented_component: Deterministic gate: invariants, scope decision, approval withholding
itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: No agent can move state directly; every consequential action passes enforce()
itu_y3172.limitations: The gate is code, not a policy language; changing it requires a code change and review.

itu_y3172.implemented_component: Simulated transport adapter with idempotency, channel authorisation and reconciliation
itu_y3172.outputs: Attempt record, provider events, delivery receipts, reconciliation outcomes
itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: REAL_NETWORK_ACCESS = False asserted in /api/health; no sockets are opened
itu_y3172.limitations: Simulation only; no real SMS/portal gateway, no carrier semantics, no delivery-report lag modelling beyond the script.

itu_y3172.implemented_component: Synthetic patient endpoint, supervisor queue, communication record

itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: Escalation tickets and documentation records persisted per case
itu_y3172.limitations: No human is actually notified. The 'patient' is a synthetic reference string.

itu_y3172.implemented_component: Orchestration engine: dispatch, context scoping, proposal resolution, audit
itu_y3172.outputs: Per-step record: assessments, gate decision, transitions, unresolved questions
itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: Documented in docs/architecture.md and exposed at /api/meta/state-machine

itu_y3172.framework_concept: Separation of ML pipeline from underlay (conceptual)
itu_y3172.implemented_component: No separate underlay: the transport simulator is in-process
itu_y3172.limitations: NOT IMPLEMENTED. ResultRelay does not implement an ML overlay/underlay split and claims no Y.3172 conformance.

itu_y3172.framework_concept: P (policy) constrained by an external legal layer
itu_y3172.framework_definition_source: ITU-T Y.3172 (06/2019) §8.1, p15 - the policy node applies policies to model output
itu_y3172.implemented_component: The policy node is implemented as deterministic rules, and the rules it may apply are bounded before ranking by jurisdiction and claim class
itu_y3172.inputs: Retrieved chunks with jurisdiction and claim_classification, plus the case jurisdiction
itu_y3172.outputs: Only AE-DU/AE-FED material may become binding for a Dubai case; other material is comparator-only and cannot reach the action
itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: 56 chunks across 13 sources of which the binding classes are confined to two jurisdictions; retriever widens a case jurisdiction upwards to the federal layer only
itu_y3172.limitations: Y.3172 says nothing about law. The mapping is architectural (where the constraint sits), not a compliance claim: a policy node that is legally bounded is still not a legal opinion.

itu_y3172.implemented_component: The proposed adviser, if enabled, runs behind the unchanged deterministic gate and can only propose; every proposal is classified PRODUCT_DESIGN_CONTROL and re-checked against the gate
itu_y3172.outputs: A proposal that the gate may reject, downgrade or mark as needing evidence
itu_y3172.evidence_of_existence: Deterministic mode is the default; the sandbox analogy is used only to describe containment, and is labelled as an analogy
itu_y3172.demonstrating_test: Not implemented - the adviser is disabled, so containment is designed and untested
itu_y3172.limitations: Art. 13 of Federal Law 2/2019 governs where such a model may run, which Y.3172 does not address. The residency question is recorded in R16 and GR-13's sibling row, and remains open.

ai_readiness.source_reference: ITU AI Readiness Report 2.0, §2, p12-13 (F2-2-ai-policy-dimension / basic framework table)
ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Standardised chunk metadata with provenance, plus typed JSON APIs
ai_readiness.evidence: 56 chunks, each with source_id, section, page, jurisdiction, classification, sha256
ai_readiness.limitations: Single internal schema; not mapped to FHIR/OMOP or any national data standard.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Provenance verification, claim classification, append-only audit chain
ai_readiness.evidence: 56/56 quotations machine-verified against official sources; hash-chained audit log
ai_readiness.limitations: Governance is bounded to the prototype's own corpus and records; no enterprise data governance process.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Public source retrieval with documented licensing boundaries; no redistribution of restricted documents
ai_readiness.evidence: source register records official URLs, licence notes and verification status for 13 sources
ai_readiness.limitations: Full texts are fetched to a local cache and not redistributed; offline use therefore degrades to the verified excerpts.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Single-container deployment; no GPU, no external model API; deterministic offline operation
ai_readiness.evidence: Application runs with FastAPI + SQLite and a static React build
ai_readiness.limitations: Infrastructure readiness is not claimed; this is a laptop-scale prototype.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: No dependency on connectivity for core workflow
ai_readiness.evidence: Retrieval and evaluation run with the network disabled
ai_readiness.limitations: Source re-verification does require network access.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Typed agent contracts, documented scoping, testable orchestration
ai_readiness.evidence: 129 backend tests covering invariants, agents, retrieval, the advisory guard, API and scenarios
ai_readiness.limitations: Skills readiness of an adopting facility is not assessed.

ai_readiness.source_reference: Report 2.0 §2 (Innovation Ecosystem indices include open source)
ai_readiness.implemented_capability: MIT-licensed source; no proprietary dependency; vendored standards excerpts kept minimal
ai_readiness.evidence: All code is in this repository under MIT; third-party text is quoted minimally
ai_readiness.limitations: No community governance, contribution process or release pipeline.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Explicit mapping to ITU-T Y.3172 concepts and to HL7 FHIR Task / IHE XDW comparators
ai_readiness.evidence: Mapping table with code locations, tests and limitations; no conformance claim
ai_readiness.limitations: Mapping is interpretive. No conformance testing against Y.3172 or FHIR was performed.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Jurisdiction-scoped evidence, classification of binding vs guidance vs comparator, human approval gate
ai_readiness.evidence: Every consequential action carries either a verified citation or a declared design control
ai_readiness.limitations: Policy coverage is limited to the reviewed corpus; it is not a compliance product.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Configurable institutional profile with labelled design controls; no invented statutory clock
ai_readiness.evidence: Clock and escalation values carry PRODUCT_DESIGN_CONTROL labels and gap references
ai_readiness.limitations: The facility has not reviewed or approved any profile value.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Synthetic-only test sandbox with seeded scenarios, replay and audit export
ai_readiness.evidence: 28 runs across 7 scenarios; replay signature comparison
ai_readiness.limitations: This is an internal test harness, not participation in a regulatory sandbox. 'Sandbox' in the reviewed framework means a supervised environment sanctioned by a regulator, which this is not.

ai_readiness.source_reference: Report 2.0 (human interaction theme); Y.3172 human supervision
ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Named supervisor role in the workflow; approval-gated corrected-result communication; escalation queue
ai_readiness.evidence: Approval required before a correction is re-communicated; withheld actions recorded
ai_readiness.limitations: Supervision is simulated. There is no authenticated supervisor identity, so the role is a field in a record rather than a person who can be held to account - the oversight is structural, not attributable, which is why this row is PARTIAL and not IMPLEMENTED.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Nothing implemented beyond language-neutral message templates and channel-agnostic design
ai_readiness.limitations: Accessibility, language and low-literacy considerations are not implemented. The Arabic/English wording of a real patient message would need clinical and cultural review.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: No generative model is invoked. The advisory boundary is implemented and tested: a model may propose, is refused if offshore or ungrounded, and can never change a gate decision
ai_readiness.code_location: backend/app/advisers/ (base, residency, guard, stub) ; backend/app/orchestration/gate.py::enforce (advisory attached after the decision)
ai_readiness.evidence: 15 adviser tests including one that asserts the gate decision is byte-identical with and without an accepted proposal; the boundary is closed by default (enable_llm=False)
ai_readiness.limitations: No model client is implemented, by design: the only adviser is a deterministic stub used to exercise containment. Generative-AI behaviour is therefore untested - what is tested is the guard.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: The applicable-instrument decision is explicit: health data is taken out of the PDPL and grounded in the ICT Health Law, which is cited for confidentiality (Art. 4), permitted circulation (Art. 16) and the 25-year retention floor (Art. 20)
ai_readiness.evidence: 13 sources, 56 verified excerpts; a Dubai case resolves to {AE-DU, AE-FED} so the federal statute is retrievable and citable, while another emirate and global material stay comparator-only
ai_readiness.limitations: Article 13 (no processing of health data outside the State without a Health Authority resolution) is recorded as a binding requirement but the prototype has no data-residency enforcement: it would run against whatever model endpoint is configured. Retention (Art. 20) and the patient-feedback duty (§4.9.10) are recorded and NOT implemented - see GR-13 and GR-14.

ai_readiness.implemented_capability: Enforced at the advisory boundary: an out-of-country endpoint is refused with Art. 13/24 cited, and a named Health Authority resolution is the only route to an offshore endpoint
ai_readiness.evidence: classify() treats .ae and loopback as in-country and everything else as out-of-country; unknown is refused
ai_readiness.limitations: The check is on the endpoint string, not on traffic; it cannot see DNS, proxies or a model bundled into a desktop app. The 25-year retention and patient-feedback duties remain unimplemented (GR-13, GR-14).

caveats: All records are synthetic. These results are not evidence of clinical safety, clinical effectiveness, or regulatory compliance.
The scenario set is authored by the same team that built the system; expected actions were written separately from engine code, but authorship is not independent of the project.
Timings are wall-clock measurements on the build machine and are indicative only.
